title: Renewing a Privileged Access Grant After PAM Rules Tightened
scenario_text:
Altair Systems controls privileged production access through its Privileged Access Management (PAM) Standard.

Version 1 (effective 2022-05-01): "A production database administrator (prod-DBA) grant may be issued for a term of up to 12 months. Grants may be renewed (extended) for successive 12-month terms upon manager approval. Password-based authentication is permitted."

Version 2 (effective 2025-01-01): "A prod-DBA grant may be issued for a maximum term of 90 days, requires a registered hardware security key, and must use just-in-time (JIT) elevation." v2 includes a transition clause: "A grant active as of December 31, 2024 remains valid under its original v1 term until that term's scheduled expiry. However, any renewal or extension of a grant executed on or after January 1, 2025 must be re-provisioned under v2 (90-day term, hardware key, JIT). Grants first issued on or after January 1, 2025 follow v2 from issuance."

The CyberArk record for grant G-6621 (engineer: P. Osei, scope: prod-DBA) shows: Original Issue Date 2024-08-10, Term 12 months, Scheduled Expiry 2025-08-10, Authentication: password. A renewal request R-6621-2 was submitted 2025-06-30 to extend the grant for another 12 months.

A security engineer posts in #access-review on 2025-07-01: "G-6621 is still riding its 2024 grant, expires Aug 10. There's a renewal request in now for another year. Can we just extend the 12-month password grant, or does the renewal force the hardware-key/90-day setup?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the CyberArk record, determine how renewal request R-6621-2 must be handled.
question: How must renewal request R-6621-2 be handled?
choices: The renewal must be re-provisioned under v2 (90-day term, hardware key, JIT), because it was submitted 2025-06-30 and v2 governs any renewal or extension executed on or after January 1, 2025.
The renewal may extend the grant for another 12 months under v1 password terms, because the original grant was issued 2024-08-10 and is grandfathered.
The grant expired on January 1, 2025 when v2 took effect, so access must be requested anew under v2 immediately.
The renewal may proceed under v1 until the 2025-08-10 expiry, after which any further access follows v2.
